summary: Foundational tools and primitive weapons for early survival.

items.description: A small pocket knife.  It isn't great for combat, but it's better than nothing.  It's sharp enough to butcher with.
A knife consisting of a long, somewhat sharpened spike and a tightly-wrapped rag as a handle.  Not as good as a real knife, but it'll do in a pinch.
A sharp knife designed for cutting meat.  It makes a poor melee weapon, but is decent at butchering corpses.
A sharp, heavy knife.  It makes a good melee weapon, and is an ideal item for butchering corpses.

A pipe with both ends bent and hammered flat to resemble a crowbar.  Use it to open locked crates without destroying them, or to lift manhole covers.  It's not strong enough to pry doors or windows, though.  You could also wield it to fight with, in a pinch.
uses: Prying quality 1: open crates/doors without explosions.

items.description: A hefty prying tool.  Use it to open locked doors without destroying them, or to lift manhole covers.  You could also wield it to bash some heads in.
A demagnetized steel claw hammer with a wooden grip.  With a hammer, nails, and planks in your inventory, you could board up adjacent doors and windows.  It has myriad other uses as well.
A Philips-head screwdriver.  It is important for almost all electronics crafting, most mechanics crafting, and has many more uses.

A small book of matches with a coarse strike surface on the outside flap for lighting them.  Allows you to use various drugs like cigarettes, light explosives like Molotov cocktails, or light nearby items on fire.  Due to the matches being lightly glued to the matchbook, they can be removed, but not replaced on the book.

A disposable plastic lighter, capable of creating a small flame with the flick of a finger.  Allows you to use various drugs like cigarettes, light explosives like Molotov cocktails, or light nearby items on fire.

A simple item for starting fires with friction between a notched plank and wooden shaft.  The shaft is spun rapidly with a sawing motion by a bowstring wrapped around it.  Very slow to acquire a usable ember.
uses: Infinite firestarter; stamina heavy but no consumables required.

items.description: A digging tool.  Use it to dig pits adjacent to your location.
A thin saw, useful for cutting through wood objects.  Activate it to turn pre-cut logs into planks.
A stone with a narrow edge affixed to a stick.  It can chop wood, but requires much more effort than a modern axe.
uses: Primitive AXE quality for chopping trees when metal axes are scarce.

items.description: A sharpened stone set into a hollowed handle.  Not nearly as usable as a proper knife, but it's better than nothing.
uses: Baseline cutting tool; enables butchering and crafting sinew.

items.description: A rock affixed to a stick in the crude facsimile of a hammer.  It functions adequately, but really can't compare to a proper hammer, and can't pull out nails either.
uses: Provides HAMMER quality for early construction without metal.

items.description: A crude shovel with a shovelhead made from wood, historically used as an alternative to metal shovels when metal was too expensive.  It works passably well, but really can't compare to a metal shovel.
uses: Allows digging pits/trenches before acquiring steel shovels.

items.description: A stout wooden pole with a whittled point.
uses: Light reach weapon useful before finding metal polearms.

items.description: A stout wooden pole with a fire-hardened point.
uses: Fire-hardened spear with better damage; combine with fire source.

items.description: A large sheet tied into a crude, over-the-shoulder sling.
uses: Crafted storage: quick + volume using spare sheets/blankets.

items.description: A long, slender wooden rod.  While traditionally intended as a training tool, it still makes a good melee weapon in a pinch.
uses: Reliable bashing weapon requiring only a 2x4 or pool cue.
